Enoch Powell (16 June 1912 - 8 February 1998) was a British politician, scholar, soldier and writer.

Franklin D. Roosevelt (January 30, 1882 - April 12, 1945), also known as FDR, was the 32nd president of the United States, serving from 1933 until his death in 1945.

Giovanni Giolitti (Italian; 27 October 1842 - 17 July 1928) was an Italian statesman who was the prime minister of Italy five times between 1892 and 1921.

Renowned for beating the Jurchen Jin with smaller armies, this Song-dynasty general, poet, and military inventor reportedly retired with scars all over his body and just four fingers remaining on both hands — who was he?
Han Shizhong (1089 - 16 September 1151) was a Chinese military general, poet, and politician of the late Northern Song dynasty and the early Southern Song dynasty.

This ancient Indian kingdom on the eastern Ganges Plain formed the core of the Mauryan and Gupta Empires and played a key role in the early development of Jainism and Buddhism — what was it called?
Magadha was a region and kingdom in ancient India, based in the eastern Ganges Plain.

A Lango politician, this man served as Uganda's first prime minister after independence in 1962, governing in coalition with President Mutesa II before a bitter rift split them. Who is he?

Milton Obote (28 December 1925 - 10 October 2005) was a Ugandan politician who served as the Prime Minister of Uganda from 1962 to 1966 and the president of Uganda from 1966 to 1971 and later from 1980 to 1985.

Fought from December 1812 to May 1814, this multinational alliance of European powers finally defeated Napoleon's empire and forced him into exile on Elba — which conflict?
War of the Sixth Coalition: 1813–1814 conflict during the Napoleonic Wars.

Convinced that Protestants and the Catholic majority had to make common cause against the Crown, this revolutionary helped found the Society of United Irishmen in 1791 and became an icon of Irish republicanism — who was he?

Rooted mostly among rural Indigenous communities in Chiapas, this Mexican far-left group has been in a frozen conflict with the state since 1994 and takes its name from a revolutionary agrarian commander — which group?
Zapatista Army of National Liberation: Far-left political and militant group in southern Mexico.
Who among these was born first?
Saint Valentine (born 175) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was born first?
Maria Goeppert Mayer (born 1906) is the earliest of the four. In 1986, the Maria Goeppert Mayer Award for early-career women physicists was established in her honor.
Which of these four is the oldest?
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is an astronomer?
Annie Jump Cannon is an astronomer.
Which of these is a mathematician?
Andrew Wiles is a mathematician. In 2018, Wiles was appointed the first Regius Professor of Mathematics at Oxford.
What is the atomic number of Plutonium?
Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
What is the atomic number of Rhenium?
Rhenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Re and atomic number 75.
In what year was Isaac Newton born?
Isaac Newton: Newton contributed to and refined the scientific method, and his work is considered the most influential in bringing forth modern science.
In what year was LSD discovered?
LSD taken orally has an onset of action of 0.4 to 1.0 hours and a duration of 7 to 12 hours.
TeX: Donald Knuth. TeX is a popular means of typesetting complex mathematical formulae; it has been noted as one of the most sophisticated digital typographical systems.
Tupolev Tu-204: Kazan Aircraft Production Association. It was developed for Aeroflot as a replacement for the medium-range Tupolev Tu-154 trijet in the 1990s.
HTML: United Kingdom. Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.
Who is credited with discovering Moscovium?
Moscovium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Moscovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mc and atomic number 115.
Who is credited with discovering Oxycodone?
Oxycodone: Martin Freund. It is a highly addictive and commonly abused drug.
Who is credited with discovering Germanium?
Germanium: Clemens Winkler. Germanium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ge and atomic number 32.
Bred for strength and endurance to haul heavy loads across the snow, this large sled-dog breed shares its arctic heritage with breeds like the Siberian Husky and Samoyed — what breed is it?
Alaskan Malamute is a large breed of dog that was originally bred for its strength and endurance to haul heavy freight as a sled dog.
Famed for foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry, this French mathematician was also a principal founder of the secretive Bourbaki group — who was he?
André Weil (6 May 1906 - 6 August 1998) was a French mathematician, known for his foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry.
This deciduous shrub genus in the rose family comes in black, red, and hybrid purple berry varieties, all bitter enough to usually be processed rather than eaten fresh — which genus?
Aronia is a genus of deciduous shrubs, the chokeberries, in the family Rosaceae native to eastern North America and most commonly found in wet woods and swamps.
These nocturnal blood-feeding insects from the genus Cimex can trigger skin rashes, itching, and even psychological distress from their bites — what are they commonly called?
Bed bug are insects from the genus Cimex, which are parasites that feed on blood, usually at night.
Native to North America and introduced to Europe in the 1930s, these prostrate shrubs in the genus Vaccinium range from 4 inches to 13 feet tall — what fruit is it?
Blueberry are a widely distributed and widespread group of perennial flowering plants with blue or purple berries.
Which winged insect fluttered into the fossil record around 56 million years ago and reaches adulthood only after pupating inside a chrysalis?

Butterfly are winged insects from the lepidopteran superfamily Papilionoidea, characterised by large, often brightly coloured wings that often fold together when at rest, and a conspicuous, fluttering flight.
Combining science, aesthetics, and technique, this field is the study and practice of making and using maps to communicate spatial information — what field is it?

Cartography is the study and practice of making and using maps. The fundamental objectives of traditional cartography are to:

Set the map's agenda and select traits of the object to be mapped.
Made of DNA wound around histone proteins, this substance shapes chromosomes into their distinctive forms during cell division and gatekeeps access to genes for transcription and repair — what is it?
Chromatin is a complex of DNA and protein responsible for condensing and packaging chromosomal DNA.
Known in the US as 'konk,' this sea snail's family includes so-called 'true' species identified by their long spires — what is it?
Conch is any of a number of different medium-to-large-sized sea snails.
Unrelated to poor hygiene, this scalp condition causes flaking and mild itching and is often treated with antifungal or keratolytic remedies; about half of all adults experience it. What is it?
Dandruff is a skin condition of the scalp. It can result in social or self-esteem problems.
Native to western North America, this towering conifer is also nicknamed Oregon pine or Columbian pine, though it isn't truly a pine at all — which tree?
Douglas fir (Pseudotsuga menziesii) is an evergreen conifer species in the pine family, Pinaceae.
Tissue similar to the uterine lining grows elsewhere in the body—often on the ovaries, fallopian tubes, or pelvis—affecting roughly 10% of women of reproductive age worldwide. What is this condition?
Endometriosis is a disease in which tissue similar to the endometrium - the lining of the uterus (womb) - grows elsewhere in the body.

This suborder of meat-eating mammals groups together the 'cat-like' carnivorans — cats, hyenas, mongooses, and viverrids — in contrast to their 'dog-like' counterparts in the other major suborder. What suborder is this?
Feliformia is a suborder within the order Carnivora consisting of "cat-like" carnivorans, including cats, hyenas, mongooses, viverrids, and related taxa.
Often bonded to glucose to form table sugar, this white, water-soluble simple sugar occurs naturally in honey, tree and vine fruits, and most root vegetables — name this sugar?
Fructose is a common monosaccharide, i.e.

Found in northern South America, this tarantula is the world's heaviest and longest-bodied spider, tipping the scales at over 170 grams, though a huntsman spider still beats it on leg span — what spider is it?
Goliath birdeater (Theraphosa blondi) is a large spider that belongs to the tarantula family Theraphosidae.
This usually benign tumor made of blood vessels typically appears on a baby's skin at birth or within weeks, often on the face, scalp, chest, or back, then shrinks over childhood — what is it?
Hemangioma is a usually benign vascular tumor derived from blood vessel cell types.
Sold as a 3 percent solution for the bathroom cabinet but explosive when concentrated, this oxidizer and antiseptic carries the formula H2O2 — what is it?
Hydrogen peroxide is a chemical compound with the formula H2O2.
This flowering plant genus boasts 310 species with showy blooms, some known by the common name 'flags' and a horticultural subgroup called 'junos' — what genus is it?
Iris (plant) is a flowering plant genus of 310 accepted species with showy flowers.

A civil engineer who commanded the Australian Corps in 1918, this WWI general was called by historian A. J. P. Taylor 'the only general of creative originality produced by the First World War' — who was he?
John Monash (27 June 1865 - 8 October 1931) was an Australian military commander of the First World War and a civil engineer.

Named after a French mathematician but reportedly learned from his Swiss tutor, this calculus theorem evaluates tricky limits by taking derivatives of the numerator and denominator — what is it called?
L'Hôpital's rule (loh-pee-TAHL) is a mathematical theorem used for evaluating the limit of a quotient of two functions, each of which tends to zero or infinity, by taking each function's derivative.
This common, soft, movable, painless growth made of fatty tissue usually forms just under the skin, often on the back, shoulders, or abdomen — name this benign tumor?
Lipoma is a benign tumor made of fat tissue. The first use of the term "lipoma" to describe these tumors was in 1709.

Located partly outside the body and partly within the pelvis, this set of sex organs includes the testicles, which produce sperm to fertilize an egg during conception — which body system is being described?
Male reproductive system consists of a number of sex organs that play a role in the process of human reproduction.
A waxy crystalline compound from peppermint and corn mint, it triggers a cooling sensation and works as a mild local anesthetic to soothe a sore throat — what is it?
Menthol is a monoterpenoid organic compound that occurs naturally in the oils of certain plants in the mint family, such as corn mint and peppermint.
Classified by carbon count into trioses, pentoses, hexoses, and more, these colorless, water-soluble simple sugars are the basic building blocks of carbohydrates — what are they called?
Monosaccharide (from Greek monos: single, sacchar: sugar), also called simple sugars, are a class of organic compounds usually with the formula (CH2O)x.
Composed of a renal corpuscle and a renal tubule, this microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney numbers between 1 and 1.5 million per healthy adult kidney — name it?

Nephron is the minute or microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney. The renal corpuscle consists of a tuft of capillaries called a glomerulus and a cup-shaped structure called Bowman's capsule.
Yellowing, thickening, and a nail separating from its bed are telltale signs of this fungal infection, far more common in toenails than fingernails — what's the medical name?
Onychomycosis is a fungal infection of the nail. Onychomycosis, also known as tinea unguium, is a fungal infection of the nail.
Combining medicine with comedy, this physician organizes volunteers to clown around for orphans and patients worldwide through a nonprofit institute he founded in 1989 — who is he?
Patch Adams (born May 28, 1945) is an American physician, comedian, social activist, clown, and author.
This bird genus, part of the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae, encompasses the living flamingo species — which genus?
Phoenicopterus is a genus of birds in the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae.

First domesticated by ancient peoples of the Iranian plateau roughly 5,000 years ago, this deciduous shrub bears a fruit rich in symbolic and mythological meaning across many cultures — name the fruit?
Pomegranate (Punica granatum) is a fruit-bearing, deciduous shrub in the family Lythraceae, subfamily Punicoideae, that grows to between 1.5-5 metres (5-16 ft) tall.
Like a cosmic lighthouse, this highly magnetized, rapidly rotating neutron star is only visible from Earth when its beam of radiation sweeps directly toward us — what's the object?
Pulsar (pulsating star, on the model of quasar) is a highly magnetized rotating neutron star that emits beams of electromagnetic radiation out of its magnetic poles.

One of the rarest and most valuable precious metals, this hard, corrosion-resistant transition metal with only one naturally occurring isotope is prized for enhancing jewelry — what's the element (symbol Rh, atomic number 45)?
Rhodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rh and atomic number 45.
Arising from connective tissues like bone, cartilage, muscle, and fat, this rare cancer of mesenchymal cells makes up just 1% of adult diagnoses but 15% of childhood ones. What is it?
Sarcoma is a rare type of cancer that arises from cells of mesenchymal origin.
Despite its long-nosed, mouse-like look, this small mammal is actually a closer cousin to hedgehogs and moles than to rodents — what is it?
Shrew (family Soricidae) are small mole-like mammals classified in the order Eulipotyphla.
Doctors examine the color of this coughed-up airway mucus — greenish or yellow tints can hint at infection, though not which organism caused it — what is it?
Sputum is mucus that is coughed up from the lower airways (the trachea and bronchi).
This Polish far-right entrepreneur and tax advisor placed third in the 2025 presidential election while chairing a libertarian party and co-leading a far-right coalition — who is he?
Sławomir Mentzen (born 20 November 1986) is a Polish far-right politician, entrepreneur and tax advisor.
A parasitic arachnid roughly 3 to 5 millimeters long that feeds on the blood of mammals and birds, with fossils dating back some 100 million years to the Cretaceous — which creature?
Tick are parasitic arachnids of the order Ixodida.
This broad category of large, hoofed mammals was reclassified in 2001 into a new clade after genetic data revealed the older grouping wasn't a true evolutionary lineage. Name the category of animals?
Ungulate are members of the diverse clade Euungulata, which primarily consists of large mammals with hooves.
This German hunting-dog breed, recognized in 1891, is so much a working dog that in its homeland it's considered unsuitable simply as a house pet — name the breed?
Weimaraner is a German breed of hunting dog of medium to large size, with history going back at least to the nineteenth century.

Unlike a user interface, which links a computer to a person, this software connection lets programs talk directly to each other — and the standard describing it is called its specification. What's the three-letter term?
API: Connection between computers or programs.
Nicknamed the 'killer' variety for its aggressive defense of the hive, this hybrid pollinating insect escaped Brazilian quarantine in 1957 and reached Texas by 1990 — which insect is it?
Africanized bee: Hybrid species of bee. The African honey bee was first introduced to Brazil in 1956 to increase honey production, but 26 swarms escaped quarantine in 1957.
Also called ramsons or bear leek, this bulbous woodland plant native to Eurasia is a wild cousin of onion and garlic — what is it?
Allium ursinum: Species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.
Comprising more than 140 species across 16 genera, this small, oily forage fish is found everywhere from the Atlantic to the Black Sea — what is it?
Also known as Umbelliferae and including carrots, celery, parsley, and dill, this plant family also contains dangerously toxic members like poison hemlock and giant hogweed — which family?

One of its founders, James Keeler, said this science 'seeks to ascertain the nature of the heavenly bodies... rather than their positions or motions' — studying everything from the Sun to the cosmic microwave background. What field is it?
Sitting at the bottom of the forebrain and including the striatum and substantia nigra, this cluster of brain nuclei governs voluntary movement and habit formation — what is it called?
Basal ganglia: Group of subcortical nuclei involved in the motor and reward systems.
Also known as vitamin B7, this B vitamin is found in every living cell and is popularly sold as a supplement; isolated, it's a white needle-like crystal — what is it?
Biotin: Chemical compound and essential nutrient.

Completely dependent on humans for reproduction after millennia of selective breeding, this domesticated moth's caterpillars produce the raw fiber behind a 5,000-year-old Chinese industry — which species?
Bombyx mori: Moth mainly used in the production of silk.

Prescribed under the tongue, as a cheek film, an injection, a skin patch, or an implant, this opioid treats pain and opioid use disorder — often combined with naloxone in Suboxone to deter injection misuse. What is it?
Buprenorphine: Opioid used to treat pain and opioid use disorder.
Called 'rockmelon' in Australia and 'spanspek' in South Africa, this orange-fleshed true melon goes by yet another name in North America — what fruit is it?
Cantaloupe: Variety of melon. Originally, cantaloup referred to the true cantaloupe or European cantaloupe with non- to slightly netted and often ribbed rind.
Sold under the brand name Rocephin, this injectable third-generation antibiotic treats everything from meningitis to gonorrhea — which drug?
Ceftriaxone: Antibiotic medication. Ceftriaxone, sold under the brand name Rocephin, is a third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic used for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
Found across North America (and one Siberian species in Asia), these small striped squirrels stash food in their cheek pouches to store for winter — what are they?
Also known as a trefoil for its three-part leaves, this legume has been farmed for over 1,000 years to fix nitrogen in soil, and a rare four-leaf version is considered a good-luck charm — what plant?
Spanning information theory and cryptography at one end and hardware design at the other, this field is broadly described as the study of computation, information, and automation — what is it?
Computer science: Study of computation. Algorithms and data structures are central to computer science.
Their Latin name means 'those with shells,' and this mostly aquatic group includes crabs, lobsters, krill, barnacles, and mantis shrimp — what are they?
Named for a 19th-century British mathematician, this pair of logic rules shows how 'and' and 'or' swap places under negation — what are they called?
De Morgan's laws: Pair of logical equivalences.

Previously known as multiple personality condition and popularized (inaccurately) by the case of 'Sybil,' this controversial mental health diagnosis is characterized by the presence of two or more distinct personality states known as 'alters' — which condition is this?
Dissociative identity disorder: Mental illness with multiple personality states.
Its leaves and flowers are covered in dense white hairs that shield it from Alpine cold and UV rays, making this daisy-family flower a symbol of mountaineering purity — what is it?
This outermost skin layer ranges from about 31 micrometers thick on delicate areas to nearly 600 micrometers on the sole of the foot — what is it?
Epidermis: Outermost of the three layers that make up the skin.

One of the few birds known to pass the mirror test, this highly intelligent corvid found across the northern reaches of Eurasia has a nidopallium proportionally as large as a chimpanzee's brain — which bird is it?
Eurasian magpie: Species of bird. The Eurasian magpie or common magpie (Pica pica) is a resident breeding bird throughout the northern part of the Eurasian continent.
Reproducing via spores rather than seeds or flowers, this group of vascular plants unfurls from coiled 'fiddleheads' into fronds and numbers over 10,000 species — what are they?
Fern: Class of vascular plants. The group includes about 10,560 known extant species.
With atomic number 87 and a most stable isotope whose half-life is just 22 minutes, this alkali metal is the second-rarest naturally occurring element on Earth — which one?
Francium: Chemical element with atomic number 87 (Fr)

Sold under a non-proprietary name once the original patent expires, this type of medication shares the same active ingredient as its brand-name predecessor, though packaging and coloring may differ — what's it called?
Generic drug: Pharmaceutical equivalent to a brand-name product.
First selectively bred for color in imperial China over 1,000 years ago, which popular aquarium pet has become an invasive pest after being released into rivers in North America and Australia?
Goldfish: Freshwater fish common in aquariums.
Born Herman Mudgett and dubbed the 'Beast of Chicago,' this con artist and serial killer worked his most notorious crimes around the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition — who was he?
H. H. Holmes: American con artist and serial killer (1861–1896)
Dubbed 'the Gauss of modern mathematics,' this French polymath's work on the three-body problem uncovered the first chaotic deterministic system, laying the groundwork for chaos theory — who is he?
Henri Poincaré: French mathematician, physicist and engineer (1854–1912)
With red compound eyes set wider apart in females, this insect lays batches of about 100 eggs on decaying matter that hatch into maggots — which species?
Housefly: Species of insect. The housefly (Musca domestica) is a fly of the suborder Cyclorrhapha.
Distinguished by the male's large, transversely ridged curved horns, which wild goat species roams Eurasia and Africa?
This 12th-century polymath from Mesopotamia wrote a treatise describing 50 ingenious mechanical devices, including his famous elephant clock, earning him the title 'father of robotics' — who is he?
Ismail al-Jazari: Muslim engineer and artist (1136–1206)
Once an assistant to astronomer Tycho Brahe and later imperial mathematician to Emperor Rudolf II, this polymath formulated the laws of planetary motion — who was he?
Johannes Kepler: German astronomer and mathematician (1571–1630)
Named from a Tongan and Marquesan word meaning 'bitter,' this pepper-family plant's ground root becomes a ceremonial Pacific Islands drink that numbs the mouth — what is it?
Kava: Species of plant. Kava or kava kava (Piper methysticum: Latin 'pepper' and Latinized Greek 'intoxicating') is a plant in the pepper family, native to the Pacific Islands.
A genus of 47 flowering plant species in the sage family, prized for its fragrant oil and used in traditional medicine, cosmetics, and as a culinary herb across Mediterranean climates — which genus?
Lavandula: Genus of plants. Lavandula (common name lavender) is a genus of 47 known species of perennial flowering plants in the sage family, Lamiaceae.
Also known as the deer ked, this blood-sucking fly sheds its own wings once it lands on a host and burrows through the fur to feed — what species is it?
Lipoptena cervi: Species of fly. Lipoptena cervi, the deer ked or deer fly, is a species of biting fly in the family of louse flies, Hippoboscidae.
Often a complication of cancer treatment, this incurable, progressive swelling condition is managed with compression therapy and manual drainage rather than diuretics — what is it?
Lymphedema: Swelling due to a compromised lymphatic system.
A student of Marie Curie, this French physicist discovered the element francium in 1939 and later became the first woman elected to the French Académie des Sciences — who was she?
Typically occurring between ages 45 and 55, this natural decline in estrogen and progesterone permanently ends a woman's menstrual periods?
Menopause: Time when menstrual periods stop permanently.
Nicknamed 'Foxbat' by NATO and built largely from stainless steel, this Soviet interceptor still holds the altitude record for an airbreathing piloted aircraft at 38 km — which jet?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-25: Family of interceptor and reconnaissance aircraft.
Drawn from the latex of opium poppies, this naturally occurring opiate acts straight on the central nervous system to dull pain — but risks dependence and tolerance. What is it?
Morphine: Pain medication of the opiate family.
Sold as Aleve, this NSAID eases pain, fever, and menstrual cramps for up to twelve hours, and also comes in a more soluble sodium form — which drug?
Naproxen: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to treat pain.
Known informally as bedwetting, this involuntary condition rarely stems from a specific medical cause and is often treated with alarms or hormone therapy — what is it called medically?
Nocturnal enuresis: Involuntary urination while asleep.

Born out of military planning before World War II, this branch of applied mathematics uses optimization and statistics to find the best possible outcome for real-world decisions — what field, sometimes called management science?
Operations research: Discipline concerning the application of advanced analytical methods.
Also called the corn poppy or Flanders poppy, this red flowering weed has symbolized remembrance in the Commonwealth since World War I — what plant is it?
Papaver rhoeas: Species of flowering plant in the poppy family.
By learning to synthesize hormones from plant sterols — even wild Mexican yams — this research chemist laid the foundation for cortisone and the birth-control pill. Who was this pioneer?
Percy Lavon Julian: American research chemist (1899–1975)
This mathematical constant, roughly 3.14159, expresses the ratio of a circle's circumference to what?
The number pi is a mathematical constant approximately equal to 3.14159, the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter. It appears in many formulae across mathematics.
Named from the Latin word for 'bridge' after Italian anatomist Costanzo Varolio, this brainstem structure sits above the medulla and below the midbrain — what is it?
Pons: Part of the brainstem in humans and other bipeds.
Named after a Russian explorer and reintroduced to Mongolia's steppes after going extinct in the wild, this rare equine has 33 chromosome pairs instead of the usual 32 — what species is it?
Colorless and odorless, this radioactive noble gas with atomic number 86 is a decay product of radium and eventually settles into stable isotopes of lead?
Radon: Chemical element with atomic number 86 (Rn)
Made up of 12 paired bones plus the sternum and spine, this bony enclosure of the chest shields the heart and lungs while housing the muscles used for breathing — what is it?
Rib cage: Bone structure of the thorax.
Originally conceived as a jet trainer before its role expanded to supersonic strike and reconnaissance, this Anglo-French attack aircraft is today flown only by the Indian Air Force. What is it?
SEPECAT Jaguar: French/British attack aircraft. It was also later license produced by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited in India for use of the Indian Air Force.
After early family-friendly Christian games found little success, which developer switched to horror in 2014 and created a hit franchise of horror video games?
Scott Cawthon: American video game developer (born 1978)

Adapted from the Army's Black Hawk with folding rotor blades and a hinged tail to fit aboard ships, this twin-engine Navy helicopter handles everything from anti-submarine warfare to medical evacuation — which aircraft?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Sikorsky SH-60 Seahawk: Naval helicopter series of the H-60/S-70 family.
Native to the tropical Americas and a cousin of the cherimoya, which spiny fruit smells like pineapple and tastes like strawberries and apple with a sour citrus tang?
Soursop: Tropical fruit tree. Soursop (also called graviola, guyabano, and in Hispanic America guanábana) is the fruit of Annona muricata, a broadleaf, flowering, evergreen tree.
In this eye disorder, the two eyes fail to align properly on the same object, which can cause a lazy eye and lost depth perception if it persists through much of childhood. What condition is it?
Strabismus: Eyes not aligning when looking at something.
Commonly known as the pork tapeworm, this parasite completes its life cycle by cycling between human waste, pig feed, and undercooked pork — which species?
Taenia solium: Species of tapeworm. Taenia solium, the pork tapeworm, belongs to the cyclophyllid cestode family Taeniidae.
This Hungarian-American aerospace pioneer made crucial advances in supersonic and hypersonic airflow, and the agreed boundary of outer space — the "___ line" — bears his name. Who was he?
Theodore von Kármán: Hungarian-American mathematician, aerospace engineer and physicist (1881–1963)
Marketed as Topamax, this oral medication treats epilepsy and prevents migraines, though it can cause weight loss and kidney stones as side effects — what is it?
Topiramate: Medication used to treat epilepsy and migraine.
Spread by body lice, chiggers, or fleas depending on the strain, this group of bacterial diseases causes fever, headache, and rash, and is treated with the antibiotic doxycycline — what is it?
Typhus: Group of infectious diseases. Typhus, also known as typhus fever, is a group of infectious diseases that include epidemic typhus, scrub typhus, and murine typhus.
Posthumously awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 1972, this physicist and astronomer is regarded as the father of his country's space program — who is he?

Vikram Sarabhai: Indian physicist and astronomer. Often regarded as the "Father of Indian space program", Sarabhai was honored with Padma Bhushan in 1966 and the Padma Vibhushan (posthumously) in 1972.
Known also as the gnu, this African antelope comes in black and blue varieties whose lineages split roughly a million years ago — which animal?
Wildebeest: Genus of antelope. Wildebeest (WIL-di-beest;, VIL-,), also called gnu (NOO or, NEW), are antelopes of the genus Connochaetes and native to Eastern and Southern Africa.
Released from prison in June 2025, this Turkish politician resumed leading the nationalist Victory Party after previously serving as deputy leader of the MHP — who is he?
The symbol for radon is Rn. Radon is a chemical element; it has symbol Rn and atomic number 86.
